clue.text: Dreadful description of a snowman?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the yeti is known as the ... Snowman

explanation.surface: A wry question about how one would describe a snowman, apparently a terrible one.
explanation.walkthrough: The yeti of the Himalayas is popularly called the Abominable Snowman, so the adjective is its standard description.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abominable is loathsome or very bad, a direct synonym for dreadful.

clue.text: Skilled actor Idris on the rise?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading the name from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: Idris Elba, the British actor

explanation.surface: A compliment to actor Idris Elba, whose career is climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent or capable, a plain synonym for skilled.

clue.text: Working with the condition of a racecourse is continuous

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
the going is the state of the ground in horse racing: firm, soft, heavy

explanation.surface: A racing report noting that work on the track's surface never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing the going is the official description of the turf, from firm to heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is still in progress without a break, so it is continuous.

clue.text: Colourful parts of manuscripts — some are found in Blackpool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the painted decorations and initials of medieval books
second meaning: the Blackpool ..., the seaside town's famous autumn light displays

explanation.surface: Bright illustrated manuscripts, some of which turn up in a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is an English seaside resort whose Illuminations are miles of decorative lights along the promenade each autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Illuminations are both the gilded decorations of old handwritten books and festive displays of electric lights.

clue.text: One who burns or stains all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a messy person who either burns things or leaves stains everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately sets fire to property, so is a person who burns things.

clue.text: Type of lettuce to have when wool-gathering?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... lettuce, a small salad leaf
second meaning: young sheep are what you would need to gather wool, taking wool-gathering literally

explanation.surface: Which salad leaf to eat while daydreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: Wool-gathering usually means daydreaming; read literally it is collecting fleece, which needs sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's lettuce, also called corn salad, is a salad green; lambs are young sheep that give wool.

clue.text: Southern sweet potato

parts.note: pud, short for pudding, is the British word for a dessert or sweet course

explanation.surface: Naming a sweet potato from the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet potato' reads as one vegetable but splits: sweet is the pudding, potato the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Vessel, reportedly complete, in cave

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

indicators.note: as it is said aloud, so a word sounding like the one for complete is entered

parts.note: whole means entire or complete

explanation.surface: An intact pot, so they say, found in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a deep natural shaft or cavern in limestone, explored by cavers.

clue.text: Cook hailed buns and cheese

indicators.note: to cook something is to prepare or doctor it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for a chef who greeted some bread rolls and some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person in the kitchen; here it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a strong blue-veined cheese from Denmark.

clue.text: The French girl is above board

parts.note: le is French for the
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Vouching that a French young woman is honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means open and lawful, so it matches legal, permitted by law.

clue.text: Rubbish spilt on me — idiot!

indicators.note: rubbish here is a nonsense jumble, telling you the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a clumsy person who has dropped waste all over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as the stuff that was spilt; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or gullible person, a synonym for idiot.

clue.text: Legal document involved part settlement (though not married)

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the following abbreviation is to be left out of the preceding word

parts.note: taken as written, losing its M before joining the anagram

explanation.surface: A legal paper covering part of a settlement for an unmarried couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters patent are an open document from a monarch or government granting a right, title or patent.

clue.text: Almost entirely missing: amount I prepared as defensive measures?

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are rearranged
nearly all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened by one letter
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a quantity they made is nearly all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as figurative: vaccinations defend the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Immunisations protect the body against disease, a medical kind of protective step.

clue.text: Insect maybe, with head in a peak?

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax
taken as written
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A bug, perhaps, with its head stuck in a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hill top in the English West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees and other insects carry pollen between flowers, so an insect is one example of a pollinator.

clue.text: Instrument is first of equipment to sort out

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: its opening letter is the one used

explanation.surface: A musician's guide to sorting out gear, starting with the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise something is to arrange it in order, an equivalent of sorting out.

clue.text: This could create repetition, concerning part of speech

parts.note: a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about how some words cause repeated sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Latin-derived 'about', used in business letters for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echo effect that repeats sound in music recordings.

clue.text: Criminal, Joker, catching Batman at last

indicators.note: the jester's word surrounds the letter taken from the hero, as if holding him

parts.note: a gagster is a joke-teller

indicators.note: only the final letter of the hero's name is used

parts.note: its final letter is the one used

explanation.surface: Batman's archvillain the Joker finally captures the caped crusader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' brings Batman's enemy to mind, but here it simply means a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised gang of violent lawbreakers.

clue.text: Checks back street one metre initially in length

indicators.note: the whole string that follows is read backwards
only the opening letter of metre is used, and the signal carries on over the next two words

parts.note: its opening letter is the one used
the opening letters of in and length, the same signal for first letters carrying on

explanation.surface: Measuring a road backwards, a metre at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' serves both metre and the two words after it, so the reversed string is street, one, then three first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Limits as a verb means restricts or curbs, so it matches checks in the sense of holds back.

clue.text: Encountered Mr Solo, perhaps, on ecstasy — what a gas!

parts.note: met means encountered
Han Solo is the smuggler in Star Wars, so Han is an example of a Mr Solo

explanation.surface: Meeting Han Solo while on drugs would be quite a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a common slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy. 'What a gas!' sounds like delight but defines literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a flammable natural gas, so the exclamation is literally pointing at a gas.

clue.text: She's very domestic and organised: has a fur uniform!

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to be rearranged
Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: A tidy homemaker who keeps a fur coat as her uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A hausfrau is a German-style housewife devoted to homemaking, so the definition describes such a woman.

clue.text: More impolite about late princess, becoming more red-faced?

indicators.note: the comparative word goes around the name of the princess

parts.note: ruder means more impolite
Princess Diana, who died in 1997

explanation.surface: Someone ruder about Diana gets more embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is the usual crossword name for the late Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddier means having a redder, healthier glow, as a flushed face does.

clue.text: Go in a Lada and turn wildly, showing such force

indicators.note: doing something wildly is doing it in a disorderly way, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: these four words supply most of the letters to be rearranged
the remaining letters, taken as written; and is a link

explanation.surface: Driving a Lada with reckless turns, like an armed militia.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lada is a Russian car. The anagram fodder skips the word and.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Guard is a US military reserve force, and the clue's driving fits such a body.

clue.text: A way in, you could say, for love?

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: a door is a way in

explanation.surface: Asking whether an entrance is a route to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply.

clue.text: Mammals climbing? That makes you guess

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: bats are flying mammals

explanation.surface: Seeing animals scaling a wall leaves you puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt, a guess.

clue.text: Bus maybe providing delight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bus is an example of public ...
second meaning: ... also means rapture, intense delight

explanation.walkthrough: Transports of delight is a stock phrase, here split into its two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a means of transport, and to be in transports is to be carried away with joy.

clue.text: Throw out some contents of the Victory?

indicators.note: only part of the phrase's letters are taken, running across the two words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the and the start of Victory

explanation.surface: Clearing out part of what is aboard Nelson's flagship Victory.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory is Nelson's ship, preserved at Portsmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant, putting them out of the property.

clue.text: Creature returns to get plant

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a deer is one example of a creature

explanation.surface: An animal comes back to fetch some vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing in water or marshes.

clue.text: Beat idol?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a throb of the heart, a heartbeat
second meaning: an attractive celebrity who makes fans' hearts flutter

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, a heart throb is simply one beat of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is a famous person adored by fans, and also, literally, a pulse of the heart.
